theater: 耶路撒冷聖殿山與上城

battle.name: 朱迪亞內戰
battle.theater: 耶路撒冷聖殿山與上城
battle.brief: 公元前93年，希姆尼王位在兩兄弟間開戰：希律尼斯二世結西頓總督安提帕特奪取耶路撒冷城內，唯聖殿山仍由亞里斯托布二世一系固守，圍城、飢荒與羅馬干預相繼而來。卡面的科林斯青銅盔屬公元前7世紀的希臘工藝，此時僅見於軍官與儀仗裝束；它的代價正是全正面開眼者只能靠隊形活。

kit.name: 科林斯青銅盔
kit.history: 全正面開眼的青銅盔。看得見的代價是：戴它的人只能靠隊形活。

countries: 這場戰爭是希姆尼王朝在朱迪亞王國內部的一場王位與大祭司之爭，交戰雙方都出自亞歷山大·雅奈烏斯家族。希律尼斯二世一方以安提帕特為軍師，得到伊杜邁安人與西頓總督的支持，並在流亡中獲得托勒密王朝埃及的援助；亞里斯托布二世一方則以耶路撒冷聖殿的祭司集團為核心，控制聖殿山與上城，僱用希臘式方陣步兵與攻城工程兵，後來又得到納巴泰王國的支援。雙方的常備骨幹都是希臘僱傭兵與本地徵召兵：希律尼斯一方以伊杜邁安輕步兵、猶太弓手與投石手為主，聖殿一方則倚靠封閉的聖殿區、城垣與工程器械作戰。外來力量的介入決定了戰局走向——羅馬共和國的元老院與駐敘利亞行省的部隊，先後用一份命令終止了圍城，又在公元前63年以軍事干預為這場內戰收尾。
countriesEn: This war was a contest inside the Hasmonean dynasty over the throne of Judaea and the office of high priest, and both sides descended from the family of Alexander Jannaeus. The camp of Hyrcanus II counted Antipater the Idumaean as its military organizer, drew on the support of the Idumaeans and of the governor of Sidon, and obtained Egyptian aid from the Ptolemaic dynasty while in exile; the camp of Aristobulus II was built around the priestly class of the Temple of Jerusalem, held the Temple Mount and the upper city, employed Hellenic phalanx infantry and siege engineers, and later received backing from the Nabataean kingdom. The standing core of both armies consisted of Greek mercenaries and locally raised levies: Hyrcanus's side fought with Idumaean light infantry, Judean archers and slingers, while Aristobulus relied on the enclosed Temple precinct, its walls and its artillery. Foreign intervention decided the course of the fighting. The Senate and the Roman forces stationed in the province of Syria ended the siege with a single order, and in 63 BC Pompey closed the civil war out with a military intervention.
people: 亞歷山大·雅奈烏斯（公元前103年至公元前76年在位，約瑟夫斯則記他統治三十三年）是這場風暴的根源：他與前妻所生的長子亞里斯托布二世、以及後妻所生的幼子希律尼斯二世，爭的是王位與大祭司職。皇后薩洛美·阿利山德拉在丈夫死後主政約九年，指定幼子希律尼斯繼承大祭司與王位，等於把兄長亞里斯托布排除在權力核心之外。亞里斯托布一系隨後以耶路撒冷聖殿為據點奪權，得到祭司階層的支持；希律尼斯反而因為不爭祭祀而得到百姓擁護，卻失去了土地與軍隊，兩兄弟的競爭由宮廷政變升級為全面內戰。真正左右戰局的是伊杜邁安人安提帕特：他以「西頓總督」的身分替希律尼斯經營軍隊、籌措資金、主持圍城，後來其家族在羅馬人的支持下掌握了朱迪亞的實權。聖殿方面的主事者是祭司階層與以利亞撒·本·哈南一類的聖殿領袖；亞里斯托布二世則派出密使尼可勞·達馬斯克赴羅馬陳情。羅馬方面，蘇拉在亞細亞戰場上以致元老院與敘利亞同僚的書信介入，龐培則在公元前63年以軍事行動解決了亞里斯托布一系的抵抗。約瑟夫斯是本役主要史料來源，他偏向希律尼斯一系，同時又批評希律尼斯在取勝後的處置。
peopleEn: The roots of the storm lay with Alexander Jannaeus, king from 103 to 76 BC, though Josephus, by his own count, credits him with thirty-three years of rule. His elder son by his first wife, Aristobulus II, and his younger son by a later marriage, Hyrcanus II, both claimed the throne and the high priesthood. The queen Salome Alexandra governed for about nine years after her husband's death and installed the younger son Hyrcanus as high priest, which cut Aristobulus out of the centre of power. Aristobulus' party then seized the Temple at Jerusalem with the backing of the priesthood, while Hyrcanus, who had not contested the ritual itself, kept the loyalty of the people but lost land and troops; the quarrel between the two brothers thus escalated from a palace coup into a full civil war. The man who actually turned the tide was Antipater the Idumaean, who as governor of Sidon organized Hyrcanus's army, its money and the siege, and whose family would later hold the real power in Judaea under Roman sponsorship. On the Temple side the decisions belonged to the priestly hierarchy and to leaders such as Eleazar ben Hanan, while Aristobulus sent the diplomat Nicolaus of Damascus to Rome to argue his case. On the Roman side, Sulla intervened through letters to the Senate and to his colleagues in Syria while campaigning in Asia Minor, and Pompey ended the resistance of Aristobulus' faction in 63 BC. Josephus is the principal source for the whole affair; he leans toward Hyrcanus while also criticizing what Hyrcanus did once he had won.
kits: 卡面這件科林斯全正面青銅盔是公元前650年前後的希臘工藝：額部開兩個圓眼孔，兩側有護頰，正面只留一道狹窄的鼻樑開口，整個人從眉骨到下顎都被包住。到了公元前93年，這種全正面盔在希臘世界早已不是野戰裝備——野戰兵員早已改用阿提卡式、卡爾基迪式與弗里吉亞式的輕便頭盔，還有給高盧僱傭兵用的蒙特福特諾式。希臘方陣步兵在朱迪亞戰場上真正會帶上陣的，是奧利匹克式或阿提卡式頭盔；全正面科林斯盔只會出現在軍官與儀仗隊伍裡，如同希姆尼王朝錢幣上那頂被學者解讀為「大祭司之盔」的希臘式頭盔圖樣，說明的是身分而不是實戰。裝具方面，希臘方陣步兵用圓盾、多利矛與短劍，身披亞麻布甲或青銅甲；希律尼斯一方的伊杜邁安輕步兵用標槍、小圓盾與投石索，猶太弓手與投石手補充遠程火力；亞里斯托布一方守聖殿，倚重弓弩、配重式投石機、石砲、撞錘與拒馬，把聖殿自身的庫藏與軍械庫當作補給核心。攻城一方另有圍牆與壕壘的土木作業器材，以及大批勞役搬運石材、填壕、築台。騎兵在朱迪亞的內戰中角色有限，但安提帕特與希臘僱傭兵都保有馬匹，用以襲擾、包抄與運載投射武器。
kitsEn: The Corinthian helmet on the card is Greek work of about 650 BC: two round eye openings in the brow, cheek pieces at the sides, and only a narrow opening at the nose, so that the whole face is covered from brow to jaw. By 93 BC this fully enclosing type was long out of use in the Greek world as field equipment. Fighting men had already moved to lighter helmets of Attic, Chalcidian and Phrygian type, together with the Montefortino pattern used by Gallic mercenaries. The phalanx infantry who actually marched in Judaea took the field in Olympian or Attic helmets; the fully faced Corinthian helmet survives only on officers and in ceremonial processions, like the Greek helmet depicted on Hasmonean coinage, which scholars read as the helmet of the high priest and which marks status rather than combat. For equipment, the Greek phalanx troops carried round shields, doru spears and short swords, wearing linen or bronze armour; Hyrcanus' Idumaean light infantry used javelins, small round shields and slings, with Judean archers and slingers adding long range fire; Aristobulus' men, defending the Temple, relied on bows and crossbows, counterweight stone throwers, bolt shooters, rams and chevaux-de-frise, treating the Temple's own treasury and armory as the core of their supply. The besiegers also needed the earthwork materials for a circumvallation wall and ditch, and large numbers of labourers to carry stone, fill the ditch and raise platforms. Cavalry played a limited part in the Judaean civil war, but Antipater and the Greek mercenaries all kept horses, for raids, envelopment and the transport of artillery.
tactics: 整場戰爭的戰術主軸是攻堅與封鎖，而不是野戰對決。圍城方先把耶路撒冷城切成兩半：以土壘與壕溝封住通往聖殿山的上坡通道，切斷上城與外城（市場區）之間的往來，再用配重式投石機與弩砲壓制城頭射界，逼近牆根後才改用撞錘與挖地道。守軍則利用聖殿區的狹窄通道與階梯，把進攻人數壓成單列，用弓弩與反制工程在缺口處反擊；約瑟夫斯記載圍城者曾向聖殿範圍內射箭，祭司以儀式潔淨為由反對，於是守方拆開牆縫讓箭矢落地收集，說明圍攻方在試探守軍的規矩邊界。飢荒是最終的攻城手段：封閉的聖殿區靠存糧與井水撐了數季，最後以餓降告終，期間守方曾試過出城反擊，一度突破封鎖線。整體特徵是「工程兵主導、圍城絞殺、靠外力收尾」：羅馬只需一道元老院命令與一批駐敘利亞的部隊，就能讓僵持數年的圍城提前結束；這說明在公元前1世紀末，真正決定朱迪亞命運的不是雙方的陣形，而是羅馬、埃及與納巴泰的資源。若以卡面那頂科林斯全正面盔來看，它最吃緊的地方正在這裡：全正面開眼，使戴盔者在狹窄街道、階梯與亂軍之中幾乎瞎掉，唯一的保障是身旁的密集方陣；而在聖殿山這種處處斷續的地形，方陣隨時散架。
tacticsEn: The tactical axis of the whole war was siege and blockade rather than a pitched battle. The besiegers first cut Jerusalem in two: an earthwork wall and a ditch sealed the uphill approach to the Temple Mount and severed movement between the upper city and the lower market quarter, then counterweight stone throwers and bolt shooters suppressed the defenders' firing from the wall heads, and only at the foot of the walls did they switch to rams and sapping. The defenders used the narrow passages and stairways of the Temple precinct to reduce the attackers to single files, answering with bows and counter-engineering at the breaches. Josephus records that the besiegers shot arrows into the area of the Temple, that the priests objected on grounds of ritual purity, and that the defenders then opened a gap in a wall so the arrows could fall and be collected, which shows the besiegers testing the limits of the defenders' own rules. Famine was the final siege weapon: the sealed Temple district held out through several seasons on stored grain and wells, and in the end it surrendered to hunger, while the defenders attempted a sortie at one point and briefly broke the blockade. The overall pattern is engineering-led, siege-grinding, and settled from outside. Rome needed only a senatorial order and a batch of troops in Syria to end a siege that had dragged on for years, which shows that in the late first century BC what decided Judaea's fate was not the formations of the two sides but the resources of Rome, Egypt and Nabatea. Seen through the Corinthian helmet on the card, the difficulty is exactly here: the fully faced eye openings leave the wearer nearly blind in narrow streets, on stairways and in a broken melee, and the only protection left is the dense formation at his shoulder, a formation that comes apart at once on the broken ground of the Temple Mount.
data: 可核的數字主要出自約瑟夫斯的記述。第一，圍城餓降的代價：他記上城因飢荒而崩潰，被困其中的死亡與失序總數記為一萬一千人左右（此為史料記載的總數，含守軍與被圍的非戰鬥人員），獲准帶著家眷離城者約二千四百人；同一組數字也說明守方是靠封閉與存糧拖到極限，而不是靠戰鬥反敗為勝。第二，羅馬的介入沒有留下可核的殘存兵力數目，但敘利亞方面配合希律尼斯行動一事有明確記載。第三，公元前63年龐培進入耶路撒冷後取走聖殿庫藏，約瑟夫斯記為約二千塔蘭特的白銀；他沒有動用聖殿的器皿，只把這筆財富視作羅馬的戰利品。行政層面，羅馬此後按人頭課徵所謂的「聖殿稅」，文獻常以每人每年兩德拉克馬記載，用以維持對耶路撒冷與聖殿的控制。距離與時間上，圍城自入冬起延續到翌年，羅馬的干預在公元前88年前後，龐培的介入在公元前63年，最終的行政重劃也在同年完成。軍隊總人數方面，雙方都沒有留下可靠的記載，只能從工程器械的規模、存糧消耗與城防長度反推，這是一場以殘兵與糧道對峙的持久戰。
dataEn: The verifiable figures come mainly from Josephus. First, the cost of the siege by hunger: he records that the upper city collapsed, with the number of those who died and were lost inside it put at about eleven thousand, a total from the sources that covers fighting men and non-combatants alike, and that about two thousand four hundred were allowed to leave with their wives and children. The same pair of figures shows that the defenders held out through enclosure and stored grain rather than through any successful counter-battle. Second, the Roman intervention left no verifiable surviving troop numbers, but the fact that the forces in Syria cooperated with Hyrcanus is explicitly recorded. Third, when Pompey entered Jerusalem in 63 BC he carried off the Temple treasury, which Josephus puts at about two thousand talents of silver; he did not touch the sacred vessels and treated the wealth simply as Roman booty. On the administrative side, Rome afterwards levied a so-called Temple tax on a per head basis, commonly recorded in the sources at two drachmas per person per year, to keep control of Jerusalem and of the Temple. As for distance and time, the siege ran from the winter into the following year, the Roman intervention came around 88 BC, Pompey's intervention in 63 BC, and the final redrawing of the administration in the same year. No dependable figures survive for the size of either army, and they can only be inferred from the scale of the artillery, the rate of grain consumption and the length of the defences: this was a war of endurance fought by remnants and along supply lines.
cause: 起因是希姆尼王朝的繼承制度本身。亞歷山大·雅奈烏斯兩次婚姻留下的兩個兒子，把王位與大祭司職都當作應得的份子；老王死後，遺孀薩洛美·阿利山德拉主政約九年，指定幼子希律尼斯二世繼承大祭司與王位，等於把兄長亞里斯托布二世排除在權力核心之外。亞里斯托布一系隨後以耶路撒冷聖殿為據點奪權，得到祭司階層的支持；希律尼斯反而因為不爭祭祀而得到百姓擁護，卻失去了土地與軍隊，兩兄弟的競爭由宮廷政變升級為全面內戰。外部條件同樣關鍵：希律尼斯在埃及的托勒密王朝與伊杜邁安人安提帕特那裡找到靠山，亞里斯托布則在阿拉伯的納巴泰王國找到支持；希臘化的宮廷傳統、希臘僱傭兵與希臘化的官制，則讓這場內戰自帶「文明之爭」的光圈——後世常把它讀成希臘化派與本土派之爭，但約瑟夫斯的敘事把重點放在王位繼承與聖殿控制上，並未把雙方簡單劃成兩種文化的代表。需要說明的是，戰爭列表把本役記在公元前93年，約瑟夫斯則把希律尼斯回國與圍城的日子分別記在公元前92年與公元前91年前後，兩者相差一二年；本卡沿用列表所標的年份。
causeEn: The cause was the succession system of the Hasmonean dynasty itself. The two sons left by Alexander Jannaeus's two marriages both treated the throne and the high priesthood as shares due to them. After the old king died, his widow Salome Alexandra governed for about nine years and named the younger son Hyrcanus II as heir to both the priesthood and the crown, which pushed the elder brother Aristobulus II out of the centre of power. Aristobulus' party then took its position at the Temple of Jerusalem with the support of the priesthood, while Hyrcanus, who had not contended for the rituals themselves, kept the favour of the people but lost his land and his soldiers, and the rivalry of the two brothers escalated from a palace coup into open civil war. The external conditions mattered just as much: Hyrcanus found patrons in the Ptolemaic court of Egypt and in the Idumaean Antipater, while Aristobulus found them in the Arab Nabataean kingdom. The Hellenic character of the court, the Greek mercenary armies and the Hellenized administration gave the war the appearance of a clash of civilisations; later writers often read it as a contest between Hellenizers and nativists, but Josephus puts the weight on the succession and on control of the Temple, and does not reduce the two parties to representatives of two cultures. One point of dating should be noted: the war list places this conflict in 93 BC, while Josephus dates Hyrcanus' return and the siege to about 92 and 91 BC respectively, a difference of a year or two; this card follows the year given in the list.
impact: 直接後果是希姆尼王朝的獨立時期在此終結。朱迪亞從一個可以自己徵稅、自己僱兵的希臘化王國，變成羅馬體系下的一個受管單位：公元前63年龐培重劃疆界，把猶太分成數段交由不同的羅馬軍政長官管轄，加利利一帶交給安提帕特；希律尼斯二世保留大祭司與「民族領袖」的名分以及部分稅權，但軍隊與外交自主權被切斷，聖殿的庫藏被帶走，神殿的經濟地位第一次被羅馬直接觸碰。安提柯二世這個羅馬扶植的傀儡王，以及安提帕特家族的崛起，是更長的後果：公元前40年左右希律尼斯二世去世後，安提帕特以安提柯三世的名義攬權，兄弟兩人相繼被羅馬處決，安提帕特的兒子希律安在公元前37年出任朱迪亞總督；朱迪亞的行政與稅制就此在希律安名下定型。長期看，這套羅馬直接統治的安排——西頓的駐軍、按人頭的稅、聖殿稅、偶像崇拜的引入——累積了深刻的怨恨，公元66年的猶太大起義，幾乎每一項都是這場內戰留下的結構性問題。
impactEn: The immediate consequence was the end of the independent period of the Hasmonean dynasty. Judaea, a Hellenized kingdom that levied its own taxes and hired its own soldiers, became an administered unit inside the Roman system. In 63 BC Pompey redrew the boundaries, dividing Judaea into districts placed under different Roman military and civil governors and leaving Galilee to Antipater. Hyrcanus II kept the titles of high priest and ethnarch together with part of the tax revenue, but the autonomy of his army and his diplomacy was cut off, the Temple treasury was carried away, and the economic position of the Temple was for the first time touched directly by Rome. The longer consequences were the puppet king Antigonus II maintained by Rome and the rise of the house of Antipater. After the death of Hyrcanus II around 40 BC, Antipater took power in the name of Antigonus III, the two brothers were executed in turn by Rome, and Antipater's son Herod became governor of Judaea in 37 BC; from that point the administration and taxation of Judaea were fixed in the name of the Herodian house. In the long run, the arrangements of direct Roman rule, the garrison at Sidon, the head tax, the Temple tax and the introduction of the worship of the emperor accumulated deep resentment, and almost every element of the great Jewish revolt of 66 CE was a structural problem left behind by this civil war.
result: 戰術上，這場內戰以圍城與飢荒收場，而不是以決定性的會戰見分曉。公元前91年前後，希律尼斯一方的伊杜邁安聯軍與希臘僱傭兵封住聖殿山，守方靠封閉與存糧抵抗數季，最後因饑荒而崩潰，約二千四百人得以帶家眷離城，亞里斯托布二世被俘並在希律尼斯手中被處死。公元前88年蘇拉的干預替希律尼斯一系掃清了羅馬方面的障礙；公元前83年，納巴泰王阿雷塔斯四世趁朱迪亞內部空虛出兵，圍攻耶路撒冷，亞里斯托布之子安提柯二世被俘殺。公元前63年龐培入城，亞里斯托布二世被押往安提阿處決，聖殿庫藏被運走，希律尼斯二世成為羅馬認可的大祭司與民族領袖，朱迪亞的政權形式由此改變。結果的深層含義是：這場戰爭沒有解決誰來做朱迪亞的問題，只是把答案從希姆尼家族手裡，轉到了羅馬元老院與代理人安提帕特家族手裡；安提柯二世這個被扶植卻無實力的傀儡王，正是公元66年大起義的導火線之一。
resultEn: Tactically, the civil war ended in a siege and a famine rather than in any decisive battle. Around 91 BC the Idumaean-led army of Hyrcanus, with Greek mercenaries, sealed the Temple Mount; the defenders held on for several seasons on enclosure and stored grain, and in the end collapsed from hunger, some two thousand four hundred being allowed out with their families, while Aristobulus II was taken prisoner and put to death in the hands of Hyrcanus. In 88 BC the intervention of Sulla cleared the Roman obstacle out of the way for Hyrcanus' party. In 83 BC the Nabataean king Aretas IV marched in on the emptiness inside Judaea and besieged Jerusalem, and Antigonus II, the son of Aristobulus, was captured and killed. In 63 BC Pompey entered the city, Aristobulus II was taken to Antioch and executed, the Temple treasury was carried off, and Hyrcanus II became the high priest and ethnarch recognized by Rome, so that the form of government in Judaea was changed. The deeper meaning of the outcome is that the war never settled the question of who would rule Judaea; it only moved the answer out of the hands of the Hasmonean house and into those of the Roman Senate and its local agent, the house of Antipater. The powerless puppet king Antigonus II, raised and used by Rome, was one of the triggers of the great revolt of 66 CE.
